notes.title: On a Journey of Retribution!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e5acfdb2b7b24e4ec0eb5245e46521ea4877e581.png[/img]
[i]The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest[/i] follows the story of a disgruntled vampire hunter on a journey of "righteous" retribution! When Simon Quest was on the brink of achieving the glory of defeating Dracula, his vampire-hunting rival swooped in and defeated the Count before he had a chance!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/176e4c3f9b0b5c82ceaf83c53106ce4f6f5710ba.png[/img]
Unwilling to be considered the “second-rate” living in his rival’s shadow, Quest decided to do the one thing no vampire hunter would ever even THINK of: resurrecting Dracula!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/651170a5308d28222e65d5a8003c347f91e2fcc3.png[/img]
But in order to do so, Simon will have to collect several artifacts related to Dracula, gathering them together to restore the Count to his full power--ripe for Simon to defeat him!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/f14ef49c291fa41247e306647ee1f8350a1b46e7.png[/img]
So, how could there possibly be any unforeseen consequences for raising the most fearsome vampire back from the dead? Nothing, right? …Right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/17d018457265d1b21b491d3bc5fa6d3c4c360eed.gif[/img]
Stay tuned for even more updates as we continue on with development!

notes.title: Taking a PEEK Inside Bram Mansion!
notes.content:
While The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest continues its development, take a peek inside Bram Mansion–one of the many different places you can visit on your journey for vampire-hunting glory!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/2fe37f3d60aba15a0ac878eb53c11918413c67d9.png[/img]
Look, you can’t be a professional vampire hunter if you’re afraid of the dark…and Skelebones!

Inside Bram Mansion, you’ll find creepy ghouls who aren’t welcoming of guests! Luckily for you, as an expert vampire hunter, you should have no problem fighting your way through all of them, right? Right!

notes.title: Whipped Into Shape!
notes.content:
Every vampire hunter needs a good weapon at their side! That's why Simon Quest’s preferred tool of destruction is a whip! Easy to deploy, quick to inflict damage, and useful across different terrains!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/3637b3dbc591c7db61caa3bef23ca6902bf7979c.gif[/img]

When dealing with enemies Simon will perform one swing each time you press the Attack button. Pressing it multiple times will  allow him to do more swings in a row. Punish enemies that get too close!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/b3aac77b38bd2999d2faf25391c267c5fab67336.gif[/img]

You can also use your whip to swing across open ledges! Time it right and you’ll latch onto a high object and swing across! Just be sure you jump down at the right time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e48d165cfd87ad404ccaff90661f2a4cdfe3fe46.png[/img]

As you travel further into your adventure, you’ll be able to upgrade your whip to take on different forms! Be on the lookout for any upgrades you can find in shops and at other points during your journey!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/80b9830a7a27bfb1fe2b3c1546ccfd03c8a32e83.png[/img]

Stay tuned for even more!

notes.title: The Classicvania You WISH You Played Before!
notes.content:
Taking inspiration from classic titles is an age-old practice when it comes to making games–especially modern retro ones!

In The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ), players will certainly appreciate the motifs, themes, and color palette in-game harkening back to familiar titles of the past! Following the story of vampire hunter Simon Quest, players will embark on a journey across the world to raise the evil Count Dracula from the dead–all for the sake of obtaining the glory stolen by rival Van Helsing!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/651170a5308d28222e65d5a8003c347f91e2fcc3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e5acfdb2b7b24e4ec0eb5245e46521ea4877e581.png[/img]
Gameplay sees players controlling Simon as he traverses numerous environments, each complete with their own brand of menacing monsters!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/a74f6f29f4ee44e4fd788f2d31713a5797151922.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/3637b3dbc591c7db61caa3bef23ca6902bf7979c.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/4e831da05b698fbdd142c4f8539808911fc10072.gif[/img]
As a skilled vampire hunter, Simon is equipped with a deadly whip, which he can use to dispatch enemies, activate spawn point lanterns, or swing across wide gaps!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e48d165cfd87ad404ccaff90661f2a4cdfe3fe46.png[/img]
In each town you visit, you’ll be able to purchase items at shops using coins obtained from slain enemies in the overworld! You’ll also have the chance to equip new subweapons, which can be deployed during combat to add an extra layer of offense! Potions that restore your health are also available to purchase, so be sure to collect those coins!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/8e98151fa84c7bab94ac7fe8cc038666410ee9f1.png[/img]
Within each mansion, you’ll find strong bosses that will challenge your skills as a vampire hunter! Keep your distance and throw a couple of daggers, or get up close and take several swings with your whip! Eliminating these bosses will grant you a piece of the evil Count, which you’ll need to collect to accomplish your ultimate goal!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/f14ef49c291fa41247e306647ee1f8350a1b46e7.png[/img]
And the experience doesn’t stop there! Across the overworld, you’ll be able to play minigames that can be discovered at certain locations! Play a crane game, a card game, or try your luck at fishing! When the going gets tough, you’ll want to unwind from all that adventuring with minigames!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/6e9372e099e0caf4053fb3c662a2a050f4c8a213.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/6668f8ddba822b0f358c41586eae0d176d0d48bc.png[/img]
And stay tuned for even more features in The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ)!

notes.title: Ask And Ye Shall SAVE PROGRESS!
notes.content:
Saving in TASQ is a simple endeavor!

In every town, you’ll encounter different monsters that appear and attack only at night! Luckily, you can enter a church to seek refuge!

Along with having their own shops, towns will have a church you can use to rest through the night (and avoid having to battle any ghastly ghouls), or save your progress. Interact with the angel statue inside churches to do so.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e9f2c6b5a6fcf8a1ae6aae11fc1755bcd25e3bcb.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/ced17221bef8ba1f094bef654c14ac89410b488f.gif[/img]
For those who do not wish to face the monsters prowling around certain towns, you can always choose to sleep through the night by talking to one of the nuns inside the church. 

At least monsters can’t get inside!...right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/22cab2ad3b6add6c92aa3802e90d3c19a7c43d3f.gif[/img]
Look forward to even more as we continue with development!

notes.title: Giving 'Em a Good KICK!
notes.content:
Don't feel like using your trusty ol' whip to dispatch your foes? Not willing to jump over them and let bygones be bygones? Then try using a good KICK!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/588317423f855131f37ff07a7bf90ac385d3dfe8.gif[/img]

Reminiscent of a mechanic from certain retro games, this sliding jump kick allows Simon to move quickly to the left or right--with an animation some players may find familiar!

Simon can even use this maneuver to dispatch common enemies, specifically Skelebones!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/24e0276a58b1730baac63c592e933c5d5333b60e.gif[/img]

You can also make use of this as a means of dodging enemy attacks, like the flail attack from this boss!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/3526861d7f5f347e8c1d8189b99928c560453a8d.gif[/img]

Look forward to making good use of this sliding jump kick to take down Skelebones or escape peril in a flash...or, just do it because it looks cool!

notes.title: Entering the Mansion!
notes.content:
Mansions are prime locations for all things monstrous, creepy, and dangerous! But to access these foreboding structures, you’ll need to complete the respective quests in each new region!

In Bram, for instance, you’ll need to do a little searching to find the mansion’s key!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/5a65317802be26806553708eb28a9411165a7103.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/8bd5ee2f1888fc77dc9a46bd042824cba1b12465.png[/img]
As defined by lead developer Programancer: “Requirements are different depending on the mansion…Generally, the idea is you get what you need to enter a mansion by completing each town’s little quests.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/2a07166d4cd5a953ad2e306086e2244e8e4fe543.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/367e5567f2eb9862a5fc6196faa4ce1cd098fac7.png[/img]
Upon completing a region's mansion quest, you'll be able to access it and take on the monsters within! Don't forget to grab enough hearts to use your subweapons and stock up on gold to prepare beforehand!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/65f69b57efd313ae5c2109714988346a76a2642c.gif[/img]

You can look forward to encountering all the different mansions, and expect to discover different methods of entering each mansion on your Transylvania adventure!

notes.title: Looking Through the Lens #2
notes.content:
We’re back with the second half of our interview with Joe, our inhouse video editor! 

[h3][b]How do you think the atmosphere and story distinguishes itself from Prison City and Dumpy & Bumpy--another one of Programancer's games?[/b][/h3]

[b]Joe[/b]: This is Programmancer’s horror game opus. Nothing in this game is short of that electric passion and care that Programmancer puts into all of his projects. Along with his signature sprinklings to make everything pop, this is most certainly a fan of these games creating a game, and sparing no expense.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/c162c0a01410ba7c8a9427e57d3807efaa0cf5d1.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/4e23120783af4aa32fe0217919d8774d1f1395a3.png[/img]

[h3][b]You don't have to get into any specific details, but do you think TASQ has opened up some future content ideas for you as a video editor?[/b][/h3]

[b]Joe[/b]: It absolutely has! Whether I get a chance to bring all of those ideas to fruition is to be seen, but not only is it in my wheelhouse, but it’s like it was made for me. Especially being a creator as a whole, not just video editing, but the design, aesthetic, and even filmmaking portion that goes along with the marketing and overall branding for this game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/0e20d1e142f41b725b002670044016c45ef311fe.png[/img]

[h3][b]From what you've seen or played so far of TASQ, what are some things you can hint at that players may get excited for?[/b][/h3]

[b]Joe[/b]: Let me make it clear that I am in love with this game. If you’re a fan of the NES style Castlevania’s, this is the ultimate experience. Not only does it capture the atmosphere of those games, but dare I say improves upon them in almost every way. It’s an absolute blast to play with plenty of easter eggs, side quests, gameplay extras, whip lashing, and beastie thrashing to go around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/76df7b44584bc7f23ab899cbce3cde8f18d3aba7.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/d80c9330afc22ec8738c298a229540950aa243e7.png[/img]

notes.title: Looking Through the Lens!
notes.content:
Our inhouse video editor, Joe, shares his insights into working on making content for The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest! Take a look!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/2c3e64567fdf20ee6ca4cd942a248e59057c5c03.png[/img]

[h3][b]So, here we are working on The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest! As a video editor, how does it feel to go from working on Prison City to TASQ?[/b][/h3]

[b]Joe[/b]: It's a pretty smooth transition, as both games are in the same wheelhouse aesthetically, but I'm enjoying TASQ much more, since I can connect to the source material. It's based on one of my favorite game series of all time. I'm a huge horror and retro gaming fan, so working on a modern-retro game dealing with Dracula and other devious denizens of Wallachia is very on-brand for me and a blast to be a part of.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/4e23120783af4aa32fe0217919d8774d1f1395a3.png[/img]

[h3][b]What do you think makes TASQ different and/or similar to Prison City?[/b][/h3]

[b]Joe[/b]: Again, the aesthetics are the same wherein you could look at both as "lost" games of yesteryear, and have them fit amongst your catalog all snug and cozy. However, TASQ is a different flavor than Prison City, especially when it comes to gameplay, objective, and story. It's no secret it emulates and parodies Castlevania, but it's in the best way possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/71d3062ac08f190c4cf2de10f74d95150453c1e1.gif[/img]

[h3][b]What do you think makes TASQ unique compared to similar titles you have seen or played?[/b][/h3]

[b]Joe[/b]: TASQ is Castlevania 2 on crack--plain and simple. Imagine a complete revamp (very much pun intended) of controls, world map, features, inventory, and expanded gameplay all spun into a story that is as funny as it is compelling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/88a55cb432ec00a2deb7ea9a7ed3af6f8342b751.gif[/img]

notes.title: Simon Quest Who?
notes.content:
Simon Quest is the protagonist of this adventure across Transylvania! But who exactly is he? Lead developer Programancer provides some insight into his character…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/17d018457265d1b21b491d3bc5fa6d3c4c360eed.gif[/img]
Programancer: Even though he's not given any dialogue in-game (as I prefer the player to insert their own thoughts into situations)- Simon is a bit of a lighthearted, albeit brash, and rebellious person. He raised himself from a young age as the result of a close call with Dracula, and he's hellbent on restoring his disgraced family's honor by fulfilling their legacy and duty as vampire hunters. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e5acfdb2b7b24e4ec0eb5245e46521ea4877e581.png[/img]
He's witty and clever- which helps him get out of most situations, and while people see him as a bumbling fool, he's more than capable of getting out of any situation he finds himself in. On the surface it may seem like he is simply resurrecting Dracula for selfish reasons, but maybe there's more to that than is immediately apparent- you'll just have to see!

In his creation, I've always thought of him as a bit of a Joseph Joestar- where you can't really take him seriously, but always manages to succeed much to his opponent's chagrin. The type of hero you think is a goofy, stupid moron, but ends up being extremely calculating and tactical. He's the type to throw insults and taunts at his opponents just to goad them into a reaction he can exploit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/42593b0df7c1f0a9f340531d95c6f741412523d4.gif[/img]
Look forward to even more updates as TASQ continues on with development!

notes.title: What’s All the BUZZZZ??
notes.content:
Did you know? Murder Hornets can murder you!

As their name suggests, these damn bugs will stop at nothing to buzzzz toward you and sting you to death. Luckily for you, you happen to be a (questionably?) well-trained vampire hunter, who happens to own a whip capable of keeping these flying critters at bay!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/b3aac77b38bd2999d2faf25391c267c5fab67336.gif[/img]
When strolling through the town of Lugosi at night, you’re guaranteed to run into several Murder Hornets–on the prowl for a late night snack of human flesh! Unlike other towns, such as Bram having zombies in the late hours, Lugosi will have Murder Hornets appear–likely because The Hive is located nearby.

And, like most other common monsters, killing Murder Hornets with your whip will cause them to disintegrate into flames. THAT'S how you solve Lugosi's evening pest problem!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/d25af0389d0742a8b6c2fffa5f9170e282dccbf6.gif[/img]
Stay tuned for even more updates along the way!

notes.title: Crabs on the Menu?!
notes.content:
Shellors are crab-like monsters inhabiting the underground section of the Bram Mansion. Along with several Manfish, these crustaceans hunt on top of rocky platforms, eager for their next victim!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/78a0c06338c143890e7a65fef893bc9132cf1f1b.gif[/img]
Although they tend to just move from side to side, Shellors will sometimes stop and produce columns of bubbles! While most novice adventurers may view these bubbles as harmless, they’ll knock you off your feet if you happen to crash into one while trying to hop a gap!

Or you could just…ya know…drop a ROCK on ‘em!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/4de3c5d53914c7f9d5816dc943c1462dc5a5abdb.gif[/img]
And unlike most common fiends, Shellors will require two cracks of the whip to dispatch, so don’t let up for a second!

notes.title: Lighting the Way to Respawn!
notes.content:
Across Transylvania, you’ll come across spooky-looking lanterns that will light up as soon as you walk past them for the first time (or when you return to them at a later point).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/df5d877e76ea4f81d749edf1174ed9c4d1896e8c.gif[/img]
Lanterns are helpful landmarks that serve as a checkpoint respawn location in the event you happen to die while in the overworld. Conversely, dying in mansions will cause you to start at the beginning of the section you died within. 

For lanterns, you'll respawn at the last one you passed, so be sure to…ya know, NOT die. Also! If you happen to attack a lantern enough times, their flames will go out, which means you won't be able to spawn back at that lantern. Unless, of course, you pass it again, which will reactivate it. Long story short: DON'T attack any checkpoint lantern!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/c9b5bb8c3076234bc6fcdbad8e39463e92cb809c.png[/img]

notes.title: Bugs, Bugs, Bugs Pt. 2
notes.content:
This week, we finish our discussion with Lead QA Tester Christian detailing his work on The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ)!

[h3][b]What are some unique gameplay elements that you think distinguish TASQ from similar titles?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: I'm not exactly an expert on every game in this wheelhouse, but from what I know they were trying to recapture a different era than TASQ is. TASQ is after that classic gameplay with a few modern touches for quality of life and variety, but at it's core it's trying to emulate that mid to late 80's feel. I also think TASQ is taking a comedic slant that I think is unique for the genre.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/17d018457265d1b21b491d3bc5fa6d3c4c360eed.gif[/img]
[h3][b]What are some of your favorite features in TASQ so far?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: I cannot tell you how satisfying it is for me to kill a Skelebone and then whip his head out of the air into the guy behind him. I just can't help myself; even when I have no reason to hit the skull, I will anyway! The secret routes in each dungeon are probably a more tangible feature that I should be taking. In each boss dungeon, there is actually an alternate route that leads to an entirely different boss fight for the dungeon. Also, there are a bunch of minigames to play throughout Transylvania to find. I swear, Programancer can't help himself but to just jam his games with as much content as he can manage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/a74f6f29f4ee44e4fd788f2d31713a5797151922.gif[/img]
[h3][b]What are some things you learned while QA testing Prison City that you can apply to your work on TASQ?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: I think the importance of clear communication is the main take away from working on Prison City. By the time I was doing the interview for Prison City, I had learned that, but early on it's hard to come up to someone and tell them you think they messed something up, especially when it's subjective. The bugs are the bugs; you find them, you report them, because they can't stay no matter what. But when you have an opinion on the quality elsewhere, it's important to open that line of communication, too. Maybe Programancer agrees with me and he changes it, or maybe he disagrees and explains the decision to me. Both of those results are fine, so there's no reason not to do it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/d80c9330afc22ec8738c298a229540950aa243e7.png[/img]
[h3][b]From what you've seen so far, how would you describe TASQ for those who have yet to play?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: If you look at TASQ and think "this looks like something I might like", I promise you it is. Programancer is a master at recapturing the magic and I would encourage people to give a try. There's no trick here, it looks the way it does because it's exactly like that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/b414d0b820eb3d18c1f93461242faa59166107d6.gif[/img]
And that's a wrap! Stay tuned for even more as we continue with development!

notes.title: Bugs, Bugs, Bugs Pt. 1
notes.content:
This week, our Lead QA Tester, Christian, gives a behind-the-scenes insight into what it’s like working on TASQ!

[h3][b]1. As a tester moving from Prison City to TASQ, how do you think both games play differently?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: The games play very differently, I understand why people might not get that at first, but Prison City is a much more free-moving game with being able to angle the chakram and the way jumping works. In TASQ, when you jump you're committed, once you're in the air there's nothing you can really do to change what's going to happen, save for an emergency back flip. The two games were inspired by different retro games and that is reflected in how they work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/71d3062ac08f190c4cf2de10f74d95150453c1e1.gif[/img]
[h3][b]2. Have you noticed anything similar between both games? Anything different?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: I mean they are both still in the same game genre and Programancer's brand of humor is still present. Of course, the crabbin comes back in a huge way in TASQ, for those who get that haha. Again, I'll say the differences are far more present. In Prison City, you picked individual levels and went in whichever order you preferred minus the start and end, meanwhile TASQ is a world you are traveling and exploring yourself; it all connects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/d85a1818fad2a0834abc5f7aea3a7be4f6fe0d19.png[/img]
[h3][b]3. What are some bugs you've found in TASQ so far?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: So TASQ is sort of being rebuilt by Programancer right now because the demo we've been using is a bit outdated. Those parts were pretty bug-free at this point and finding bugs in something that is about to be remade isn't exactly productive. As of right now my job has been making more suggestions, for example there is a staircase in the cave between the towns of Bram and Bela that I felt was hard to actually notice, so I asked to have it raised up so players could notice what it was easier, and boom it was done. That's a part of QA too; it's not just bugs that can make a player's time with a game worse.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/1e169b9c951f3640e7a41a5dfa6987cceff486f1.gif[/img]
[h3][b]4. How do you feel about working with Programancer once again on another project?[/b][/h3]

[b]Christian[/b]: What did I say last time? "Programancer is the man" or something like that? I'm ecstatic, he's just the best to work with. Incredibly responsive and kind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e48d165cfd87ad404ccaff90661f2a4cdfe3fe46.png[/img]
Look forward to Part 2 of our interview with Lead QA Tester Christian!

notes.title: Programancer Dev Log #3
notes.content:
We’re back this week to share a third set of insights from the TASQ lead developer, Programancer!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/17d018457265d1b21b491d3bc5fa6d3c4c360eed.gif[/img]

[h3][b]When can folks expect to get their hands on TASQ?[/b][/h3]
[b]Programancer[/b]: Depends on IF THEY WISHLIST IT.

[h3][b]Were there any mechanics you wanted to include in Prison City/TASQ but couldn't find room for them?[/b][/h3]
[b]Programancer[/b]: That's kind of hard to answer, because Prison City was born out of a want to work on a project made of things I couldn't do in TASQ, and TASQ is also something that Prison City couldn't be. They're basically the inverse of one another!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/88a55cb432ec00a2deb7ea9a7ed3af6f8342b751.gif[/img]
[h3][b]Can players expect to find any secrets or easter eggs in TASQ like in your previous work?[/b][/h3]
[b]Programancer[/b]: Almost the entirety of TASQ is a miserable little pile of secrets! But if you want to find them all, have at you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/09ff1b0cb51e5cdaaf4d6c7f3ef954d4eff5298d.gif[/img]
[h3][b]What are some goals that you envision for TASQ?[/b][/h3]
[b]Programancer[/b]: I definitely want a memorable world with lots of options. There are so many inventory items in TASQ that are optional. Don't want a knife? Get the tomahawk. Don't want the axe? How about a HAMMER? Whips not your thing? How about pugilism? 

Also just guiding the player along a path to the end naturally and organically, but letting players 'sequence break' if they're skilled into other areas is a very important thing to me. I want players to know they don't have to do anything in any order- if they want to go to the 5th mansion, they can absolutely get the prerequisites to do so instead of going to the first mansion. It's a very big game, and I want people to have different experiences they can share with other players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/71d3062ac08f190c4cf2de10f74d95150453c1e1.gif[/img]

notes.title: Programancer Dev Log #2
notes.content:
Lead developer Programancer shares more insights behind The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ)!

[h3][b]Is there a difference in core vision you have for TASQ than your other projects?[/b][/h3]

[b]Programancer[/b]: I'm very protective of TASQ, because it's something I've planned out start to finish back in 2019- I know exactly where I want it to go from the beginning of the game to the end of the game. I usually leave a lot of room for emergent design in my projects- Prison City especially had nothing but emergent design for every level, but TASQ is a different beast altogether! It's absolutely a "vision" of a game for me.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/88a55cb432ec00a2deb7ea9a7ed3af6f8342b751.gif[/img]
[h3][b]Perhaps this goes without saying, but what were some inspirations for TASQ?[/b][/h3]

[b]Programancer[/b]: People will go for the lowest hanging fruit- Castlevania- or more specifically, Classicvania, and they're not wrong! I like having a hybrid of a large world to explore coupled with linear (albeit with branching path-havin) Mansions, but my primary inspiration is Zelda! Specifically Zelda 2 and Link's Awakening. I know it doesn't look like that, but the structure of the game mirrors those. Each town/area has a quest you need to complete to gain access to the mansions- you can go to them out of order and complete those quests if you want and you're free to explore, but every region is contained to its own quest. There are also lots of little details and oddities across the world- something Link's Awakening does very well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/b414d0b820eb3d18c1f93461242faa59166107d6.gif[/img]
[h3][b]So, why did you want Simon to go on a quest for what seems to be out of spite or envy over Stan's victory over Dracula?[/b][/h3]

[b]Programancer[/b]: There's definitely more to Simon Quest's Quest (hehehhe) than it seems! There might be some personal reasons for it that aren't quite as shallow... But people will have to play to find out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/41a356bf2d1d2d181244bfa90cfe43999cd17ded.gif[/img]

notes.title: The First Lore-ific Details!
notes.content:
It’s good to have an idea of the world and the “why” when you’re on your Transylvanian adventure! Get to know some of the lore of The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ)!

****

[h3]In the year 15XX, a once peaceful Romania was in unfathomable turmoil…[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/c162c0a01410ba7c8a9427e57d3807efaa0cf5d1.png[/img]
[h3]Dracula, a long slain vampire, was once again given flesh and was sending hordes of demonic undead to pillage the land.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/4e23120783af4aa32fe0217919d8774d1f1395a3.png[/img]
[h3]A disgraced vampire hunter named Simon Quest then embarked on a journey to end Dracula's reign of terror and restore honor to his family name.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e5acfdb2b7b24e4ec0eb5245e46521ea4877e581.png[/img]
[h3]Unbeknownst to Simon, his rival had already defeated Dracula and sealed his body away into five tombs to lock his soul in Hell.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/176e4c3f9b0b5c82ceaf83c53106ce4f6f5710ba.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/f14ef49c291fa41247e306647ee1f8350a1b46e7.png[/img]
[h3]Learning he was too late, a frustrated Simon decided he should piece Dracula back together to defeat him and reclaim his lost glory.

...and so our Transylvania Adventure begins...[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/0e20d1e142f41b725b002670044016c45ef311fe.png[/img]
[h3]Look forward to even more!

notes.title: Programancer Dev Log #1
notes.content:
Following the release of Prison City, Programancer’s back cookin’ up something very special! Get a glimpse into his insight behind The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ)!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/76df7b44584bc7f23ab899cbce3cde8f18d3aba7.png[/img]
[h3][b]Well, here we are! On the road to another game! How does it feel jumping focus from Prison City to TASQ?[/b][/h3]

[b]Programancer[/b]: Feels pretty good! It was fun working on something very kinetic and action heavy like Prison City, but I want to get back to whippin' Draculas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/2c3e64567fdf20ee6ca4cd942a248e59057c5c03.png[/img]
[h3][b]What similarities do you think exists between Prison City and TASQ?[/b][/h3]

[b]Programancer[/b]: Well, I kind of started Prison City as the antithesis to TASQ- TASQ is a slow burning adventure with a lot of adventury things to do, and Prison City is a much smaller game in scope. They’re definitely two completely different animals, despite the NES-esque trappings!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/934f931f7fab33b89a653d35a6d3b6d3fd8e2a1a.png[/img]
[h3][b]Any key differences between Prison City and TASQ? Especially ones you wanted to highlight.[/b][/h3]

[b]Programancer[/b]: Where Prison City is a game all about your movement and very kinetic in nature, TASQ sees a much more deliberate approach- it has committed jumps (with some concessions for aerial mobility). Prison City is more about hitting each level and making your way to the end, but TASQ has a world that lets you explore a bit and kind of live in it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832636/e48d165cfd87ad404ccaff90661f2a4cdfe3fe46.png[/img]
Stay tuned for even more insights behind TASQ’s development with Programancer!

Be sure to follow Retroware’s publisher page to stay up-to-date on all our games, news, and more!

notes.title: A New Adventure Begins at MAGFEST 2024!
notes.content:
From Programancer, the developer of [i][b]Prison City[/b][/i] and [i][b]Dumpy & Bumpy[/b][/i], comes a brand new title: 
[h3][b]The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest![/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/17d018457265d1b21b491d3bc5fa6d3c4c360eed.gif[/img]

[h3]You’re supposed to be the hero, but your spotlight was taken away![/h3]
Your rival defeated Dracula first, now Simon Quest must embark on a journey of retribution to raise the Count from the dead piece-by-piece, slay him, and obtain the glory he deserves!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/e177be3fc6432b1c6b3f3194f7a5233e4265b8bd.png[/img]
[h3]Go on a perilous journey through the world of Transylvania. 
Explore dark mansions, discover minigames, and collect different parts of Dracula to raise him from the dead…then kill him![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/d85a1818fad2a0834abc5f7aea3a7be4f6fe0d19.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/20a7583f60581d1a50e3ce60fd060b1742ee5b37.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/e48d165cfd87ad404ccaff90661f2a4cdfe3fe46.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/55d3a3740022272187c588f027fe58f67610f138.png[/img]
[h3]Create different equipment chains and customize your experience with a host of adjustable settings![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/871811dac65663c3e87756e519a388e3126f411a.png[/img]
[h3]Wanna take a break from your journey? Enjoy a fine platter of minigames that include: Memory, Fishing, Crabbin Races, Crane Game, and even some Launch Surfing![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/3d2b93c44d1d20359440f2ddcf96f1420540c657.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/6e9372e099e0caf4053fb3c662a2a050f4c8a213.png[/img]
[h3]We’re excited to announce this new project in development with Programancer![/h3]

[h3][b]AND[/b], if you’re itching to get your hands on playing a preview of [b]The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ)[/b], YOU CAN at MAGFest 2024 at the National Harbor from Jan. 18 - Jan. 21![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29892260/4ae75f2a4248160f07d34ebfc00650448d5cb1d6.png[/img]
[h3]Look for the Retroware booths in the MIDDLE of the MIVS hall! We’ll also be featuring [i][b]Toxic Crusaders[/b][/i] right next to our TASQ booth, so be sure to stop by both![/h3]

[h3]We can’t wait to have players take their first dive into [i]The Transylvania Adventure of Simon Quest (TASQ)[/i]! Look forward to even more![/h3]
